statements.statement: A system with 99.9% availability is expected to have approximately 4.3 hours of downtime per month.
statements.explanation: A system with 99.9% availability is expected to have about 43 minutes of downtime per month, not 4.3 hours.

statements.statement: Redundancy can help improve a system's availability by having multiple instances to handle requests.
statements.explanation: Redundancy increases availability by ensuring that if one instance fails, others can take over and continue serving requests.

statements.statement: Failover mechanisms automatically switch to a backup system to improve reliability when the primary system fails.
statements.explanation: Failover enhances reliability by automatically redirecting traffic to a different instance, ensuring continuous availability even if the main instance fails.

statements.statement: Adding a single load balancer is not effective in improving system availability.
statements.explanation: Adding a load balancer helps distribute requests efficiently across multiple instances, enhancing system availability by preventing overload on a single instance.
